author: John Muir
title: The Story of My Boyhood and Youth
edition: Boston and New York: Houghton Mifflin, 1913, published March 1913. Every selected excerpt has been collated in full against the dated Boston Public Library copy digitised as Internet Archive storyofmyboyhood00muir_1. Gutenberg 18359 supplied the initial transcription but describes an undated fourteenth impression; no date is invented for that impression. The single substantive selected-word variant is resolved in favour of the 1913 witness: Chapter VIII reads ‘sent me flying to the woods’. Prose line wrapping and words hyphenated solely at line endings are rejoined; Gutenberg typographical punctuation and underscores marking italics are retained. Publisher matter, captions and navigation labels are excluded. The Library of Congress 1913 copy independently corroborates the edition date. The Hickory Hill well excerpt (Chapter VI), added in the 2026-10-07 repair, was collated at word level with the same witness and shows no word variants; its illustration caption is omitted. The library text holds all eight chapters with their printed synopses; the 1913 reading ‘sent me flying to the woods’ is applied, and the rest of the text follows Gutenberg 18359 uncollated. Captions and the index are excluded. On 2026-11-18 the whole of Chapter I (its synopsis and blocks 1–54) was collated word by word against the same witness, every difference decided on the page image: two readings changed to the 1913 text (‘plain reading- and spelling-lessons’; ‘high roaring waves. “Now where we are,”’), and the printing’s thin-spaced contractions (‘could n’t’, ‘did n’t’) are closed up as in the transcription.

rights.basis: Gutenberg explicitly identifies this eBook as public domain in the USA. Its front matter dates the text to March 1913; the Library of Congress catalog and scanned title page independently identify the 1913 Houghton Mifflin edition. All twenty selected excerpts were collated to the Boston Public Library 1913 witness (the well excerpt added in 2026-10-07 at word level), including resolution of the one substantive word variant. The original English text predates 1931; no modern added matter is selected. The later impression number is not treated as a publication date.

acquisition.method: Project Gutenberg plain text (eBook 18359, UTF-8, CRLF normalised to LF) from the PG mirror. Kept Chapters I–VIII up to THE END; removed the PG header and footer, the transcriber’s note, title and contents pages, the list of illustrations, the index, every illustration caption (each a doubled title with its legend) and the transcription’s ToC/ToList link markers. Each chapter numeral is joined with its title in a heading, followed by the chapter’s printed synopsis as a paragraph; blank-line separated paragraphs were joined with single spaces at line ends. The edition’s one collated reading was then applied in the Chapter VIII passage: “sent me flying to the woods” (PG omits “flying”). Converted by a scratch Node script; every nightly reading was located exactly.
